title: A survey of ultra-compact high-state AM CVn binaries with ZTF and Gaia: New discoveries and observational constraints on Galactic space density
comment: 19 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Ultra-compact AM CVn binaries in the high-state of stable mass transfer ($\dot{M}\gtrsim10^{-9}M_\odot/\rm{yr}$) are expected to be among the loudest persistent sources for upcoming space-based GW observatories. These systems typically have orbital periods $P_{\rm{orb}}\lesssim30$ minutes. We present a systematic search for high-state AM CVn binaries in the Milky Way by targeting a region within the Gaia color-magnitude diagram, combined with ZTF time-domain photometry. We focus on variable targets within that sample with 5-30 minute periods. Our survey discovered three new high-state AM CVn binaries (ZTF J1840-1742, ZTF J2007-0527 and ZTF J2111+3158) with orbital periods of 16.86, 18.63, and 16.71 minutes, and recovered three known systems. We obtain high-speed photometry and phase-resolved spectroscopy to confirm their nature. Their spectra show helium emission lines with no detectable hydrogen. In two targets, the lines are double-peaked, and Doppler tomograms confirm an accretion disk. We estimate mass accretion rates of $\sim10^{-9}M_\odot/\rm{yr}$, and $3σ$ X-ray luminosity upper limits of $\sim10^{33}\rm{erg/s}$. Based on this sample, we infer a local space density of high-state AM CVn population in the Milky Way of $\sim(1.0-2.7)\times10^{-8}\rm{pc}^{-3}$ (for disk scale heights $h_z=300-200$ pc), representing 2-5% of the total Galactic AM CVn density. Their birth rate, $\sim(2.4-4.3)\times10^{-4}\rm{yr}^{-1}$ (for $h_z=300-200$ pc), is consistent with the total AM CVn birth rate, implying most systems entering the high-state phase survive and evolve to longer orbital periods. This local space density suggests LISA and TianQin will detect about 36% and 19% of the total Galactic population, respectively, during their nominal 4-yr missions ($S/N\ge5$). The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST will detect about 34-44% of these systems over its 10-yr survey ($m_r\lesssim26.9$ mag).

AI.tldr: The paper reports a systematic search for high-state AM CVn binaries in the Milky Way using Gaia color-magnitude selection combined with ZTF time-domain photometry, discovering three new systems with 16-19 minute orbital periods and recovering three known ones. Based on this sample, the authors infer a local space density and birth rate for this population, and estimate that LISA, TianQin, and LSST will detect a significant fraction of these systems.
AI.motivation: High-state AM CVn binaries are expected to be among the loudest persistent gravitational wave sources for upcoming space-based observatories (LISA, TianQin), yet the population was poorly understood. The authors aim to systematically find and characterize these systems to constrain their space density, birth rate, and detectability by future facilities.
AI.method: The survey targets a specific region of the Gaia color-magnitude diagram combined with ZTF time-domain photometry, focusing on variable targets with 5-30 minute orbital periods. Follow-up high-speed photometry and phase-resolved spectroscopy were obtained to confirm the AM CVn nature of candidates. Doppler tomography was used to confirm accretion disks, and X-ray upper limits were derived. Space density and birth rates were inferred from the sample, and detection fractions for LISA, TianQin, and LSST were estimated.
AI.result: Three new high-state AM CVn binaries (ZTF J1840-1742, ZTF J2007-0527, ZTF J2111+3158) with orbital periods of 16.86, 18.63, and 16.71 minutes were discovered, plus three known systems recovered. Spectra show helium emission lines with no hydrogen; two show double-peaked lines with confirmed accretion disks. Mass accretion rates are ~1e-9 Msun/yr, with X-ray luminosity upper limits of ~1e33 erg/s. Local space density inferred as (1.0-2.7)x1e-8 pc^-3, representing 2-5% of the total Galactic AM CVn density; birth rate ~(2.4-4.3)x1e-4 yr^-1. LISA and TianQin are predicted to detect ~36% and ~19% of the total population respectively, while LSST will detect ~34-44%.
AI.conclusion: High-state AM CVn binaries represent a small but detectable fraction of the Galactic AM CVn population. Most systems entering the high-state phase survive and evolve to longer orbital periods. These systems are promising targets for future GW detectors and will be substantially sampled by LISA, TianQin, and LSST, enabling detailed population studies.

title: A comparison of best fits obtained in white dwarf asteroseismology using the WDEC and the LPCODE
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, published in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We perform the asteroseismic fitting of 4 DAVs using a grid of WDEC models with chemical pro- files that closely mimic those of the LPCODE models and compare them with published asteroseis- mic fitting results using the LPCODE (Romero et al. 2017). These 4 objects are KIC 11911480, J113655.17+040952.6, KIC 4552982, and GD1212. The similarities in the results in those controlled experiments point to a consistency in the models. Given similar input, the LPCODE and the WDEC make similar models and calculate similar periods. We further perform the asteroseismic fitting of the same 4 DAVs by relaxing the constraints on the chemical profiles. We explore the effects of different methods for weighing the modes when calculating the goodness of fit of the models, as well as the effect of only including a subset of the known period spectrum. Such numerical experiments can help place recent and future efforts in pipeline fitting of numerous DAVs and DBVs using the WDEC on firmer footing (Hall et al. 2023).

AI.tldr: The paper performs asteroseismic fitting of 4 DAV white dwarfs using WDEC models with chemical profiles mimicking LPCODE models, compares results with published LPCODE fits, verifies model consistency, then explores relaxed chemical profile constraints, different mode weighting schemes, and subset period fitting to inform future pipeline fitting efforts.
AI.motivation: To validate the consistency between WDEC and LPCODE white dwarf evolutionary models for asteroseismic fitting of DAVs, and to systematically test methodological choices (chemical profile constraints, mode weighting, period subsets) that affect the reliability and robustness of automated pipeline fitting for large samples of pulsating white dwarfs.
AI.method: Asteroseismic fitting of four DAVs (KIC 11911480, J113655.17+040952.6, KIC 4552982, GD1212) using WDEC models with chemical profiles mimicking LPCODE grids, compared against published LPCODE results. Additional fitting experiments relax chemical profile constraints, vary mode weighting schemes in goodness-of-fit calculations, and test fitting with subsets of the known period spectrum.
AI.result: Similar asteroseismic fitting results are obtained between WDEC and LPCODE models when given similar input, indicating consistency between the two stellar evolution codes. The controlled experiments demonstrate that both codes produce comparable models and period calculations under equivalent conditions.
AI.conclusion: The consistency between LPCODE and WDEC models validates their interchangeability for scientific fitting purposes. The numerical experiments on weighting schemes and period subsets provide important guidance for robustly applying pipeline-based asteroseismic fitting to large numbers of DAVs and DBVs using WDEC in future efforts.

title: Custom Colors: A Module for Computing Synthetic Photometry On-the-Fly in Stellar Evolution Calculations, Integrated with MESA and Usable with Other Stellar Evolution Codes
comment: 24 pages, 15 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Feedback welcome
summary: Stellar evolution simulations predict physical quantities such as luminosity, whereas broadband photometric observations measure flux in specific bandpasses; converting the predicted stellar state to magnitudes requires interpolating a stellar atmosphere model at the surface parameters, convolving the resulting spectral energy distribution (SED) with filter transmission curves, and applying a photometric zero-point correction. We introduce Custom Colors, which performs this conversion from the stellar model. It is integrated into MESA as MESA Custom Colors, and available as the Python package SED_Model for external applications. At each timestep, the module interpolates a user-specified atmosphere grid at the current T_eff, log g, [M/H], applies geometric dilution at a user-specified distance, convolves the SED with each requested filter transmission curve, and appends observer-frame magnitudes to standard MESA output files. We demonstrate the module across six diverse use cases: TP-AGB evolution, nonlinear RR Lyrae pulsation, starspot-modified photospheres, white dwarf cooling, blue-loop evolution, and rotational spot modulation based on an external YREC SPOTS grid. These cases draw on Kurucz/ATLAS9, BT-Settl, and Koester DA atmosphere grids and filter systems including Roman WFI, LSST ugrizy, Gaia, and extended Johnson UBVRIJHKLMN. Two of these demonstrations compare the module directly with observational data: a 0.6M_dot DA white dwarf cooling track follows the broad Gaia DR3 cooling locus from M_G ~ 8.5 to 15mag without intermediate color transformation, and an RSP model recovers the Kepler light curve of FN Lyr (KIC6936115) to 1.1% in period and 0.2% in amplitude.

AI.tldr: Custom Colors is a tool integrated into MESA (and available as the Python package SED_Model) that converts stellar evolution model predictions into observer-frame broadband photometric magnitudes by interpolating user-specified atmosphere grids, applying geometric dilution, convolving with filter transmission curves, and applying zero-point corrections. It is demonstrated across six diverse use cases including TP-AGB evolution, RR Lyrae pulsation, white dwarf cooling, and rotational spot modulation, with two case studies validated directly against observational data (Gaia DR3 WD cooling track and Kepler light curve of FN Lyr).
AI.motivation: Stellar evolution codes predict physical quantities like luminosity, but observational data come in the form of bandpass-filtered magnitudes. Bridging this gap requires converting model predictions to observable photometry through atmosphere model interpolation and filter convolution, which previously required cumbersome intermediate steps. The authors aim to provide a seamless, integrated module that performs this conversion automatically at each timestep.
AI.method: The module interpolates a user-specified atmosphere grid at the current surface parameters (T_eff, log g, [M/H]), applies geometric dilution at a user-specified distance, convolves the resulting SED with each requested filter transmission curve, and appends observer-frame magnitudes to standard MESA output files. It is integrated into MESA as MESA Custom Colors and released as the standalone Python package SED_Model. It supports various atmosphere grids (Kurucz/ATLAS9, BT-Settl, Koester DA) and filter systems (Roman WFI, LSST ugrizy, Gaia, extended Johnson UBVRIJHKLMN).
AI.result: Custom Colors successfully handles six distinct use cases spanning different stellar phases and atmosphere grids. Validation against observations shows a 0.6 solar-mass DA white dwarf cooling track matching the broad Gaia DR3 cooling locus from M_G ~ 8.5 to 15 mag without intermediate color transformation, and an RSP model reproducing the Kepler light curve of FN Lyr to 1.1% in period and 0.2% in amplitude.
AI.conclusion: Custom Colors provides a robust, flexible, and directly applicable photometric conversion capability for stellar evolution modeling, enabling direct comparison between model predictions and observational broadband photometry across a wide range of stellar types, atmosphere grids, and filter systems.

title: Further Investigation on Chromospheric Activity Patterns of the RS Canum Venaticorum Star V711 Tauri
summary: We present new long-term spectroscopic observations of the very active RS Canum Venaticorum (RS CVn) star V711 Tauri (V711 Tau), obtained during several observing runs from 2005 to 2021. By means of spectral subtraction technique, several optical chromospheric activity indicators $\mbox{Ca {\sc ii}}$ infrared triplet, H$_α$, $\mbox{Na {\sc i}}$ D$_{1}$, D$_{2}$ doublet, $\mbox{He {\sc i}}$ D$_{3}$, and H$_β$ lines, are analyzed. V711 Tau shows strong excess emission in the chromospheric activity lines, and the emission is mainly associated with the K1 IV primary component. The G5 V secondary component also shows weak emission features. There are four optical flare events during our observations, characterized by the $\mbox{He {\sc i}}$ D$_{3}$ line emission features and stronger emission in other activity lines, which have similar order of magnitude as the strong flares of other active RS CVn-type stars. We separate our long-term observations to twelve observing groups, and find that V711 Tau has two active longitudes around phases 0.25 and 0.75 to dominate the activity in most of time. The chromospheric activity level shows a long-term variation, indicating possible chromospheric activity cycle. Moreover, a close spatial connection between photospheric spots and chromospheric active regions in short and long timescale is found for V711 Tau.

AI.tldr: Long-term spectroscopic observations of the RS CVn star V711 Tau from 2005-2021 reveal strong chromospheric activity primarily from the K1 IV primary, four optical flare events, two active longitudes near phases 0.25 and 0.75, possible chromospheric activity cycles, and a close spatial connection between photospheric spots and chromospheric active regions.
AI.motivation: To study the long-term chromospheric activity of the active RS CVn star V711 Tauri using multi-epoch spectroscopic observations, characterizing its activity indicators, flares, active longitudes, and activity cycles.
AI.method: Spectral subtraction technique was applied to analyze several optical chromospheric activity indicators (Ca II infrared triplet, Hα, Na I D1/D2 doublet, He I D3, and Hβ lines) from observations spanning 2005-2021, with observations divided into twelve groups for long-term variability analysis.
AI.result: V711 Tau shows strong excess chromospheric emission mainly from the K1 IV primary (with weak emission from the G5 V secondary), four optical flare events of similar magnitude to strong flares of other active RS CVn stars, two dominant active longitudes near phases 0.25 and 0.75, long-term chromospheric activity variation suggesting an activity cycle, and a close spatial connection between photospheric spots and chromospheric active regions.
AI.conclusion: V711 Tau exhibits persistent and strong chromospheric activity with flares, stable active longitude structure, and cyclic long-term variability, while photospheric and chromospheric activity are spatially correlated across both short and long timescales.

title: Doppler-shifted Signatures in the Chromospheric Line Profiles of II Pegasi
summary: Stellar flares are frequently accompanied by prominence eruptions, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and other forms of plasma motion. Based on the long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring data set of the RS CVn-type star II Pegasi (II Peg), we search for stellar prominence eruptions and potential CMEs by investigating asymmetric signatures in the H$_α$ and H$_β$ line profiles during the flare events. We observed seven optical flares with asymmetric spectral profiles, releasing low limit energies of $10^{33}$--$10^{34}$ erg in the H$_α$ line. Five of these flares were associated with six potential CMEs, identified through the Doppler-shifted emission signatures in the chromospheric line profiles, particularly the H$_α$ line. The mass estimates for the CME candidates range from $10^{19}$ to $10^{20}$ g, while the kinetic energies are calculated to be around $10^{33}$--$10^{34}$ erg. The most massive CME candidate was simultaneously recorded in the H$_α$, H$_β$, and He I D$_{3}$ lines. For II Peg, the possible flare-CME association rate is about 30\%. There were also some redshifted excess absorption signatures in the H$_α$ line profiles. These signatures could not only be observed in the flaring spectra but also in the spectra without flare, which could be interpreted as features resulting from flare-driven coronal rain and quiescent rain, respectively.

AI.tldr: Using long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring of the RS CVn-type star II Pegasi, this study identifies seven optical flares with asymmetric Hα/Hβ line profiles, of which five are associated with six potential CMEs (masses 10^19–10^20 g, kinetic energies 10^33–10^34 erg). The possible flare-CME association rate is ~30%, and redshifted excess absorption features are interpreted as flare-driven coronal rain and quiescent rain.
AI.motivation: To search for stellar prominence eruptions and potential coronal mass ejections from II Peg by analyzing asymmetric spectral signatures during flare events, thereby advancing our understanding of stellar magnetic activity and flare-CME associations beyond the Sun.
AI.method: Analysis of long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring data of II Peg, searching for asymmetric signatures in Hα and Hβ line profiles during flare events to identify prominence eruptions and CME candidates via Doppler-shifted emission signatures.
AI.result: Seven optical flares with asymmetric profiles (Hα energies 10^33–10^34 erg); five associated with six CME candidates (masses 10^19–10^20 g, kinetic energies ~10^33–10^34 erg). The most massive CME was observed simultaneously in Hα, Hβ, and He I D3. The flare-CME association rate is ~30%. Redshifted excess absorption signatures were found in both flaring and non-flaring spectra, attributed to flare-driven and quiescent coronal rain.
AI.conclusion: II Peg exhibits a significant flare-CME association rate (~30%), demonstrating that stellar CMEs can be detected through chromospheric line asymmetries. Redshifted absorption features indicate coronal rain processes, offering insight into cool plasma condensation on active stars.

title: A matter of class and flare Flare productivity in solar active regions and power-law constraints on the flare frequency distribution
summary: Solar active regions are the source of virtually all significant space weather events, therefore the relationship between their observable properties and flare production is important to characterize. The flare productivity of solar active regions is analyzed across solar cycles 23--25 as a function of magnetic complexity, sunspot area, and solar-cycle phase. Additionally, the power-law index of the peak flux frequency distribution is estimated. The GOES soft X-ray event reports matched with daily Solar Region Summaries (SRS) are used to create a robust active region catalog. This catalog is supplemented with the 50-year HEK flare catalog and the newly released STIX flare catalog from Solar Orbiter to estimate the power-law index. Magnetically complex active regions ($βγ$, $βδ$, $βγδ$) produce the majority of M- and X-class flares while comprising only $\sim$13\% of all daily active-region observations, showing that larger flares disproportionately occur in larger area sunspots. All three catalogs can be represented with a consistent power-law index of $α= 2.02 \pm 0.01$ for the peak flux frequency distribution. However, a class-by-class analysis of the C/X and M/X flare ratios reveals that the distribution steepens significantly towards higher energies. Fitting this steepening as a lognormal tail and extrapolating two decades beyond the X-class threshold predicts a recurrence time of $370^{+292}_{-159}$~yr for an X100-class (`Carrington-type') superflare, compared to only $\sim$26~yr from a naive single power-law extrapolation. While $α\approx 2$ provides a useful global description of the flare frequency distribution, the steepening area-productivity relation and the divergence between C/X and M/X derived slopes both point to a deficit of the most energetic flares ...

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes flare productivity of solar active regions across solar cycles 23–25, correlating magnetic complexity, sunspot area, and solar-cycle phase with flare production. Using GOES, HEK, and STIX flare catalogs, the authors find a consistent power-law index of α=2.02±0.01 for the peak flux frequency distribution, but a class-by-class analysis reveals the distribution steepens toward higher energies. Extrapolating with a lognormal tail predicts a recurrence time of ~370 years for an X100-class superflare, far longer than the ~26-year estimate from a naive single power-law extrapolation, pointing to a deficit of the most energetic flares.
AI.motivation: To characterize the relationship between observable properties of solar active regions and their flare productivity, which is critical for understanding and potentially predicting significant space weather events across multiple solar cycles.
AI.method: The authors combined GOES soft X-ray event reports with daily Solar Region Summaries (SRS) to create a robust active region catalog, supplemented with the 50-year HEK flare catalog and the newly released STIX flare catalog from Solar Orbiter. They analyzed flare productivity as a function of magnetic complexity (βγ, βδ, βγδ classifications), sunspot area, and solar-cycle phase, and estimated the power-law index of the peak flux frequency distribution using multiple datasets.
AI.result: Magnetically complex active regions (βγ, βδ, βγδ) account for ~13% of daily observations but produce the majority of M- and X-class flares, with larger flares disproportionately occurring in larger-area sunspots. All three catalogs yield a consistent power-law index of α=2.02±0.01, but the distribution steepens significantly at higher energies. A lognormal-tail fit extrapolated two decades beyond the X-class threshold predicts an X100 superflare recurrence time of ~370 years, versus only ~26 years from a single power-law extrapolation.
AI.conclusion: While α≈2 serves as a useful global description of the flare frequency distribution, the steepening area-productivity relation and the divergence between C/X and M/X derived slopes point to a deficit of the most energetic flares, indicating that simple power-law extrapolations overestimate the occurrence rate of extreme solar flares.

title: Characterization of the variability of the blue supergiant HD 14134
comment: 19 pages, including 19 figures and 8 tables. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The post-main sequence (MS) evolution of massive stars encompasses phases in which the stars display high variability. One such class of objects are the blue supergiants which may be in either the pre- or post-red supergiant phase of their evolution. Their variability patterns might provide constraints for a proper classification of the objects. We aim to characterise the observed variability of the B supergiant HD14134 and to investigate the imprint of a time-variable wind on the brightness variation of the star and its impact on the detectability of pulsation signals. Spectroscopic data were collected over a 5-month period and combined with photometry from TESS. Stellar parameters were derived from modelling of the time-averaged spectrum with CMFGEN and the SED and were confirmed with stellar evolution models computed with MESA. The light curves and radial velocity curves of selected lines were analysed to determine pulsation signals. The wind variability and its imprint on the stellar brightness were investigated from an analysis of the Halpha line. Predictions of mode excitations were computed with the GYRE pulsation code and compared to the frequencies determined from the observations. A g-mode with a period of ~19.2 d and its harmonics are consistently detected in all data sets. The spectra unveil strong, non-periodic wind variability and 3 frequency signals were identified as due to this wind variability. The stellar parameters and age derived for HD14134 together with the absence of radial pulsations classify the star as a post-MS object evolving towards the red-supergiant stage, questioning its classification as alpha Cyg variable. The results reinforce that simultaneous long-term spectroscopic and photometric monitoring is indispensable for reliable frequency detections and for disentangling of variabilities imprinted by a time-variable wind from those imposed by pulsations.

AI.tldr: The paper characterizes the B supergiant HD14134 using 5 months of spectroscopy and TESS photometry, detecting a ~19.2-day g-mode with harmonics alongside non-periodic wind variability. The stellar parameters, age, and absence of radial pulsations classify it as a post-main-sequence object evolving toward the red supergiant stage, challenging its classification as an alpha Cyg variable and highlighting the need for combined long-term spectroscopic and photometric monitoring.
AI.motivation: To characterize the observed variability of the B supergiant HD14134 and to investigate how time-variable winds imprint on brightness variations, which may affect the detectability of pulsation signals and help constrain the evolutionary classification of post-main-sequence massive stars.
AI.method: Spectroscopic data collected over 5 months combined with TESS photometry. Stellar parameters derived from CMFGEN modeling of the time-averaged spectrum and SED, confirmed with MESA stellar evolution models. Light curves and radial velocity curves of selected lines analyzed for pulsation signals; Halpha line analyzed for wind variability; GYRE pulsation code used to compute mode excitation predictions compared with observed frequencies.
AI.result: A g-mode with period ~19.2 days and its harmonics were consistently detected in all datasets. Strong non-periodic wind variability was unveiled, with 3 frequency signals attributed to wind variability. Stellar parameters and age, combined with the absence of radial pulsations, classify HD14134 as a post-main-sequence object evolving toward the red-supergiant stage.
AI.conclusion: HD14134 should be reclassified as a post-main-sequence object evolving toward the red-supergiant stage rather than an alpha Cyg variable. Simultaneous long-term spectroscopic and photometric monitoring is indispensable for reliable frequency detections and for disentangling wind-induced variability from pulsation signals.

title: Cepheid metallicities from low-resolution near-infrared spectra: validation against the optical reference scale
comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Classical Cepheid metallicities trace recent chemical enrichment and help assess systematics in Cepheid-based distance measurements. They are derived mainly from high-resolution optical spectroscopy, which provides the benchmark abundance scale but limits measurements to nearby systems. Extending such studies to more distant Cepheids with extremely large telescopes requires complementary low-resolution near-infrared methods and careful treatment of model--data residuals. We test whether low-resolution SpeX/IRTF Y+J-band spectra can yield metallicities compatible with homogenised optical abundances. We analyse 14 Galactic classical Cepheids with periods of approximately 13--69 d, supplemented by two shorter-period stars from the IRTF Spectral Library. Using Bayesian full-spectrum fitting based on MARCS/TURBOSPECTRUM spectra and a regularised covariance likelihood, we infer [M/H] and compare it with homogenised optical [Fe/H]. For the primary 14-star sample, the inferred metallicities reproduce the optical reference scale with a mean offset of -0.05 dex, a scatter of 0.09 dex, and a robust scatter of 0.12 dex; the median posterior uncertainty is 0.22 dex. Including the two additional stars changes these values only slightly. Compared with a diagonal likelihood, the covariance-aware treatment reduces the mean offset and improves the stability of the uncertainty calibration. Low-resolution Y+J spectra therefore contain usable metallicity information for classical Cepheids when short-range correlated residuals and localised modelling imperfections are treated explicitly. The resulting near-infrared metallicity scale provides a practical foundation for extending Cepheid metallicity work to larger and more distant samples.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether low-resolution SpeX/IRTF Y+J-band near-infrared spectra can recover metallicities for classical Cepheids consistent with the homogenised optical abundance scale. Using Bayesian full-spectrum fitting with MARCS/TURBOSPECTRUM models and a regularised covariance likelihood on 14 (plus 2 supplementary) Galactic Cepheids, they find a mean offset of -0.05 dex and a scatter of 0.09 dex relative to optical [Fe/H], demonstrating that low-resolution NIR spectra contain usable metallicity information when correlated residuals are treated explicitly.
AI.motivation: Classical Cepheid metallicities are crucial for tracing chemical enrichment and calibrating Cepheid-based distance measurements, but current high-resolution optical spectroscopy benchmarks are limited to nearby systems. Extending abundance studies to more distant Cepheids using extremely large telescopes requires complementary low-resolution near-infrared methods, which need validation.
AI.method: The authors analyse 14 Galactic classical Cepheids (P ≈ 13–69 d) plus two shorter-period stars from the IRTF Spectral Library using low-resolution SpeX/IRTF Y+J-band spectra. They perform Bayesian full-spectrum fitting based on MARCS/TURBOSPECTRUM model spectra with a regularised (covariance-aware) likelihood, infer [M/H], and compare against homogenised optical [Fe/H]. A diagonal-likelihood variant is also tested for comparison.
AI.result: The inferred metallicities reproduce the optical reference scale with a mean offset of -0.05 dex, scatter of 0.09 dex, and robust scatter of 0.12 dex; median posterior uncertainty is 0.22 dex. Adding two extra stars changes results only slightly. The covariance-aware treatment reduces the mean offset and improves uncertainty-calibration stability compared with a diagonal likelihood.
AI.conclusion: Low-resolution Y+J near-infrared spectra contain usable metallicity information for classical Cepheids when short-range correlated residuals and localised modelling imperfections are explicitly handled. The resulting NIR metallicity scale provides a practical foundation for extending Cepheid metallicity studies to larger, more distant samples.

title: Asymmetry in the protostellar system HOPS 198: Evidence for the evolution of outflow opening angle driven by density of the surrounding core
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Protostellar outflows are thought to be responsible for the low star formation efficiency of protostellar cores. However, whether outflows can disperse a significant fraction of the gas in the core depends on the outflow opening angle. It is established that the outflow opening angle increases during the early stages of the protostellar evolution, but the underlying mechanism is poorly understood. Observations of HOPS 198, a Class 0 protostar in the Orion A molecular cloud, provide insights into this question. HOPS 198 exhibits a strong east-west asymmetry in its outflow and its core. The opening angle of the eastern lobe ($\sim80^{\circ}$) is more than twice wider than that of the western lobe ($\sim30^{\circ}$), while the surface density of the west side of the core is $1.5-2.8$ times higher than the east side. Using an analytical model in which the molecular outflow morphology is shaped by interactions between the wide-angle protostellar wind ($\gtrsim 80^{\circ}$) and surrounding material in the core, we find that the difference in opening angle for the two lobes can be explained by the difference in core density on the two sides. This result supports the hypothesis that the evolution of the outflow opening angle is driven by the evolution in the density of the protostellar core.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes HOPS 198, a Class 0 protostar in Orion A, which shows a strong east-west asymmetry in its outflow (eastern lobe opening angle ~80° vs western ~30°) and core density (west side 1.5-2.8× denser). An analytical model of wide-angle protostellar wind interacting with surrounding core material successfully explains the opening angle difference via the core density asymmetry, supporting the hypothesis that density evolution drives outflow opening angle evolution.
AI.motivation: Protostellar outflows are believed to regulate star formation efficiency by dispersing core gas, but whether they can disperse significant gas depends on the outflow opening angle. The opening angle increases during early protostellar evolution, yet the underlying mechanism is poorly understood. The asymmetric outflow of HOPS 198 offers a unique opportunity to test what drives this opening angle evolution.
AI.method: The study uses observational data of HOPS 198 to quantify the outflow opening angles (east ~80°, west ~30°) and core surface densities on both sides. An analytical model is constructed in which the molecular outflow morphology is shaped by the interaction between a wide-angle protostellar wind (≳80°) and the surrounding dense core material, to test whether the observed density asymmetry can reproduce the opening angle difference.
AI.result: The model successfully explains the factor-of-two-plus difference in opening angle between the eastern and western lobes using the observed 1.5-2.8× difference in core surface density between the two sides, demonstrating that ambient core density can control outflow collimation.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the hypothesis that the temporal evolution of outflow opening angle is driven by the evolution of protostellar core density, i.e., as the core is depleted/dispersed during protostellar evolution, the outflow widens.

title: Properties of granular light bridges
comment: 9 pages, 9 figures, and one movie related to Fig. 2. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Granular light bridges in sunspots are a manifestation of magnetoconvection in an approximately vertical magnetic field that is weaker than the field of the umbra. We study the relations between observed properties of granules and magnetic field in five strong granular light bridges located in a complex sunspot. Thermal parameters, magnetic field vector, and line-of-sight velocity were obtained from an inversion of the GREGOR spectropolarimetric scan in the lines Si I 1082.71 nm and Ca I 1083.90 nm. Sizes and lifetimes of granules were measured in a simultaneous sequence of images in the TiO band. The light bridges under study are comprised of granules spanning 0.2"-1.4" with approximately 6-minute lifetimes. The largest granular structures (> 1") are spatially correlated with 1 km/s upflows and weak, inclined magnetic fields (300 G) near the equipartition threshold. Statistical comparisons demonstrate an inverse relationship between magnetic field strength and continuum intensities, line-of-sight velocity dispersion, and effective granular diameters. These relationships vary among individual light bridges, depending on the large-scale magnetic field topology. Large expanding granules similar to the photospheric ones appear in light bridges only when the local magnetic field strength approaches the equipartition value.

AI.tldr: The paper studies granular light bridges in sunspots, combining spectropolarimetric inversions and TiO imaging to analyze granules, magnetic fields, and velocities in five strong light bridges, finding inverse relationships between magnetic field strength and intensities, velocities, and granule sizes.
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetoconvection manifests in granular light bridges where the magnetic field is weaker than the surrounding umbra, and to characterize the relations between observed granule properties and local magnetic field conditions.
AI.method: Spectropolarimetric inversions of Si I 1082.71 nm and Ca I 1083.90 nm lines from GREGOR to extract thermal parameters, magnetic field vectors, and velocities; simultaneous TiO-band imaging to measure granule sizes and lifetimes.
AI.result: Light bridge granules span 0.2"-1.4" with ~6-minute lifetimes. Large granules (>1") correlate with 1 km/s upflows and weak, inclined fields (300 G) near equipartition. Inverse relationships exist between field strength and continuum intensity, velocity dispersion, and granule diameters, varying among bridges with magnetic topology.
AI.conclusion: Large expanding granules, similar to photospheric granules, only appear in light bridges when the local magnetic field approaches the equipartition value, indicating the key role of field strength in enabling convection-driven granulation.

title: 3D simulations of a complete convective silicon shell burning phase
summary: We present 3D hydrodynamic simulations of a complete silicon shell burning phase until fuel exhaustion at the end of the evolution of a 14$M_\odot$ core-collapse supernova progenitor, using a reduced 25-isotope nuclear network. We investigate how realistic turbulent convection affects this burning phase, which has a more complicated set of nuclear reactions than previous burning phases. We find broad similarities between the 3D simulation and the 1D \textsc{MESA} model. However, due to more realistic feedback from the very stiff convective boundaries in the hydrodynamic simulations, the 3D simulation experiences lower convective boundary mixing (CMB) compared to 1D, and hence entrains less fresh fuel into the silicon shell. This leads to the silicon shell in the 3D model burning for roughly 800\,s shorter. We find that the nuclear burning timescales for the dominant reactions are faster than the mixing timescale, making this entire process a convective-reactive event. The angular-averaged energy generation profile shows a double-peaked structure, where the region between the positive peaks are close to zero, or are negative. We find that throughout the base of this silicon shell, many $(α, p)$ and their inverse reactions are important. The forward and reverse rates are very similar, so slight fluctuations in the temperature cause regions to be either exoergic or endoergic, leading to a complicated energy generation evolution. This study presents an exploration using a single reduced nuclear network, however, due to the sensitivity of this burning phase future studies should investigate the impact of more complete nuclear networks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents 3D hydrodynamic simulations of the complete silicon shell burning phase in a 14 M☉ core-collapse supernova progenitor using a reduced 25-isotope nuclear network, finding that realistic turbulence leads to less convective boundary mixing than 1D models, causing the silicon shell to burn ~800 s shorter, and revealing a convective-reactive regime with a double-peaked energy generation profile where (α,p) reactions and their inverses play key roles.
AI.motivation: To understand how realistic turbulent convection affects silicon shell burning—a nuclear burning phase with more complex nuclear reactions than previous phases—in core-collapse supernova progenitors, and to compare 3D hydrodynamic results against standard 1D stellar evolution models.
AI.method: Performed 3D hydrodynamic simulations of a complete silicon shell burning phase until fuel exhaustion in a 14 M☉ core-collapse supernova progenitor, using a reduced 25-isotope nuclear network, and compared against 1D MESA models.
AI.result: The 3D simulation shows broad similarities to 1D MESA but exhibits lower convective boundary mixing due to stiffer boundaries, leading to less fresh fuel entrainment and a ~800 s shorter silicon shell burn. The process is a convective-reactive event (nuclear burning timescales faster than mixing timescales). The angular-averaged energy generation shows a double-peaked structure with near-zero or negative regions between peaks, where (α,p) reactions and their inverses have similar forward and reverse rates causing fluctuating exoergic/endoergic regions.
AI.conclusion: The study highlights significant differences between 3D and 1D treatments of silicon shell burning, emphasizing the importance of realistic convection in determining burning durations and energy generation. It also notes the sensitivity of this phase to nuclear network choices, recommending future studies with more complete networks.

title: Tracing expansion-driven star formation in the Perseus molecular cloud using young stellar objects
comment: 14 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: $Context$. Recent studies have linked star formation in the solar neighbourhood to the expansion of the Local Bubble. The Per-Tau Shell (PTS), a vast 3D dust structure hosting the Perseus and Taurus clouds on its surface, is a candidate for such triggered formation. $Aims$. We aim to reconstruct the star formation history of the Perseus molecular cloud and investigate its potential link to the historical expansion of the PTS. $Methods$. We performed a 6D phase-space analysis of 406 young stellar objects (YSOs) of Perseus. Our approach integrates Gaia DR3 kinematics with Bayesian age inference and a heteroscedastic likelihood framework to resolve radial gradients in YSO ages and intrinsic tangential velocity dispersions relative to the PTS centre. We constructed a unified catalogue by integrating existing infrared-based classifications to examine the projected spatial segregation of different evolutionary stages and compared stellar 3D kinematics with $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO gas velocity fields to assess kinematic coherence. $Results$. The YSOs exhibit coherent outward motions relative to the centre of the PTS, a negative age-distance gradient with younger populations at larger radii, and a radial decline in tangential velocity dispersions. Younger YSO classes also show a stronger directional concentration towards the PTS centre. Both the coherent proper motions and the line-of-sight velocity gradients of these YSOs align with the gas velocity field, indicating large-scale kinematic coherence. $Conclusions$. The Perseus YSOs exhibit concordant kinematic and temporal signatures consistent with an expansion-driven origin. These results provide robust evidence for a layered, inside-out pattern of star formation, suggesting that the historical expansion of the PTS triggered a sequential progression of star birth and effectively shaped the star formation history of the Perseus complex.

AI.tldr: This study reconstructs the star formation history of the Perseus molecular cloud using 6D phase-space analysis of 406 YSOs, finding coherent outward motions, a negative age-distance gradient, and radial declines in velocity dispersions that align with gas kinematics. The results support an inside-out, expansion-driven star formation scenario linked to the historical expansion of the Per-Tau Shell.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether star formation in the Perseus molecular cloud was triggered by the historical expansion of the Per-Tau Shell, a vast 3D dust structure hosting the Perseus and Taurus clouds on its surface, building on recent findings that link solar neighbourhood star formation to the expansion of the Local Bubble.
AI.method: A 6D phase-space analysis of 406 Perseus YSOs integrating Gaia DR3 kinematics with Bayesian age inference and a heteroscedastic likelihood framework to resolve radial gradients in YSO ages and intrinsic tangential velocity dispersions relative to the PTS centre. A unified catalogue was built from existing infrared-based classifications to study projected spatial segregation of evolutionary stages, and stellar 3D kinematics were compared with 12CO and 13CO gas velocity fields to assess kinematic coherence.
AI.result: YSOs show coherent outward motions relative to the PTS centre, a negative age-distance gradient (younger populations at larger radii), a radial decline in tangential velocity dispersions, and stronger directional concentration of younger evolutionary classes towards the PTS centre. Coherent proper motions and line-of-sight velocity gradients align with the gas velocity field, indicating large-scale kinematic coherence.
AI.conclusion: The concordant kinematic and temporal signatures of Perseus YSOs provide robust evidence for a layered, inside-out pattern of star formation, suggesting that the historical expansion of the Per-Tau Shell triggered a sequential progression of star birth and effectively shaped the star formation history of the Perseus complex.

title: Binary evolution at the extremes of mass-transfer efficiency: Contact, mergers, and population signatures
comment: 14 pages + 5-page appendix, 10 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A on the 4th of August 2026
summary: Binary star evolution remains inherently uncertain, and several physical processes are not well understood. These open questions in binary physics come in addition to major uncertainties in single-star evolution, such as angular momentum transport and interior mixing. For example, the efficiency of mass transfer (MT) -- which is the fraction of transferred mass that is actually accreted -- is one of the main uncertainties in binary evolution. We present a grid of 1D binary evolution models with identical initial conditions to an earlier grid in which MT was limited by the spin-up of the accretors. Now we employ fully conservative MT, allowing for a one-to-one comparison between the two grids, and covering the full range from highly non-conservative to fully conservative MT. We explore how these two maximally different MT efficiencies change the occurrence and incidence of contact phases, stellar mergers and common envelope phases, and how they affect the present-day population of (post-)mass-transferring binaries. We find that fully conservative MT increases the incidence of contact systems by roughly a factor of 6 (from 11% to 62%), and the stellar merger incidence by more than a factor of 2 (from 16% to 38%). We also find the emergence of double-core CE phases, which are absent for lower MT efficiencies. Comparing two synthetic binary populations built using the two grids with observed Algol and stripped-star binaries reveals that even though conservative MT is favoured to reproduce the observed stripped-star binaries, the observed population of Algol binaries cannot be explained by a single MT efficiency. We conclude that the MT efficiency depends on the configuration of binary systems and cannot be described by a single value. Our work highlights the need for a better understanding of binary MT and indicates that current binary-star models are incomplete.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a grid of binary evolution models with fully conservative mass transfer (MT), compared to an earlier grid with MT limited by accretor spin-up. Fully conservative MT increases contact system incidence from 11% to 62%, mergers from 16% to 38%, and introduces double-core common envelope phases. Comparing synthetic populations to observed Algol and stripped-star binaries shows conservative MT explains stripped stars but no single MT efficiency can explain both populations, implying MT efficiency depends on the binary configuration.
AI.motivation: Mass transfer efficiency is one of the main uncertainties in binary star evolution, yet current models treat it with various assumptions. The authors aim to quantify the impact of two maximally different MT efficiencies on binary outcomes such as contact phases, mergers, and common envelopes, and to test which efficiency better matches observations.
AI.method: A grid of 1D binary evolution models was computed with fully conservative MT, using identical initial conditions to a prior grid with spin-up-limited (non-conservative) MT. The two grids were compared across outcomes (contact, merger, common envelope) and used to build synthetic binary populations that were contrasted with observed Algol and stripped-star binaries.
AI.result: Fully conservative MT increases contact incidence by ~6x (11% to 62%), mergers by >2x (16% to 38%), and produces double-core CE phases absent at lower MT efficiencies. Conservative MT reproduces observed stripped-star binaries, but no single MT efficiency can explain the observed Algol population.
AI.conclusion: Mass transfer efficiency is not a universal constant but depends on the specific binary configuration. Current binary-star models are incomplete and require a better physical understanding of mass transfer to accurately predict binary populations.

title: Augmentation of the Gauribidanur radioheliograph for observations of circularly polarized emission from the solar corona at low radio frequencies
comment: There are 25 pages with 18 figures in a manuscript. This is currently submitted to 'Solar Physics' journal
summary: The magnetic field strengths (B) in the solar photosphere are routinely measured using the Zeeman effect. However, such measurements are not available in the solar chromosphere and corona. The Gauribidanur RAdioheliograPH (GRAPH), near Bangalore in India, has been successfully carrying out total intensity (Stokes I) observations of the solar corona at low frequencies ($\lesssim$ 100 MHz) for several years now. Radio emission from the Sun in the above frequency range originates typically in the heliocentric distance r $\gtrsim$ 1.2 $R_\odot$ . We recently augmented GRAPH with the aim to observe circularly polarized radio emission (Stokes V) from solar corona, in particular, from the 'quiet' corona. Combining the low frequency Stokes I & V radio images, and modeling techniques, it is possible to calculate the magnetic field strengths in the solar corona on regular basis. This work details the procedures undertaken to augment the GRAPH for simultaneous observations of both Stokes I & V radio emission from the solar corona, and the calibration procedure. Preliminary results indicate that the augmented GRAPH can effectively detect Stokes V emission associated with thermal emission from the 'quiet' Sun at frequencies $\lesssim$ 100 MHz, in addition to Stokes V emission associated with the non-thermal radio bursts from the 'active' Sun.

AI.tldr: The paper describes the augmentation of the Gauribidanur RAdioheliograPH (GRAPH) to enable simultaneous Stokes I and V observations of the solar corona at low frequencies (<100 MHz), along with calibration procedures. Preliminary results show the system can detect Stokes V emission from both the quiet Sun's thermal emission and non-thermal radio bursts from the active Sun, enabling regular estimation of coronal magnetic field strengths.
AI.motivation: Magnetic field strengths in the solar photosphere are routinely measured via the Zeeman effect, but such measurements are not possible in the chromosphere and corona. Low-frequency radio observations of the corona offer a viable alternative path to infer coronal magnetic field strengths, which is crucial for understanding coronal physics.
AI.method: The authors augmented the GRAPH radioheliograph to carry out simultaneous Stokes I and V observations of the solar corona. They describe the augmentation procedures, the calibration pipeline, and combine low-frequency Stokes I & V radio images with modeling techniques to derive coronal magnetic field strengths. Preliminary validation was performed by detecting Stokes V emission from the quiet Sun's thermal emission and active Sun's non-thermal bursts.
AI.result: Preliminary results demonstrate that the augmented GRAPH can effectively detect Stokes V emission associated with thermal emission from the quiet Sun at frequencies below 100 MHz, as well as Stokes V emission from non-thermal radio bursts of the active Sun.
AI.conclusion: The augmented GRAPH enables regular simultaneous Stokes I and V observations of the solar corona, making it possible to routinely calculate coronal magnetic field strengths through combined imaging and modeling approaches.

title: Spherically Polarized Alfvén Waves and the Gosling Boost
summary: Alfvén waves are thought to play critical roles in solar wind acceleration and plasma heating in the solar corona and inner heliosphere. Parker Solar Probe (PSP) has highlighted the role of large amplitude Spherically Polarized Alfvén Waves (SPAWs), where the locally constant magnetic field magnitude $|\mathbf{B}|$ together with outward propagation explains the observed one sided radial velocity enhancement - the Gosling boost. Starting from the MHD equations, we derive the modified wave pressure and Poynting flux under the SPAW condition, and demonstrate both are governed solely by the transverse magnetic fluctuations. Using PSP data from Encounters 6--25, we define an unperturbed velocity baseline from the lower 10th-percentile running average and statistically characterize the radial evolution of Alfvénic fluctuations. The background solar wind velocity shows clear radial acceleration, while the velocity perturbation amplitude $δv$ decreases with heliocentric distance. This decay is anisotropic between the radial and perpendicular directions, which is a direct consequence of the growing magnetic deflection angle related to the spherical polarization. Our results demonstrate that radial velocity enhancements in the young solar wind arise naturally from SPAWs rather than from localized velocity jets, and provide direct observational evidence for the anisotropic radial evolution of SPAWs in the inner heliosphere.

AI.tldr: The paper derives the modified wave pressure and Poynting flux for Spherically Polarized Alfvén Waves (SPAWs) from MHD equations, showing both are governed solely by transverse magnetic fluctuations. Using Parker Solar Probe data from Encounters 6-25, it characterizes the radial evolution of Alfvénic fluctuations, finding that background solar wind accelerates while velocity perturbation amplitude decreases anisotropically with heliocentric distance. The results show radial velocity enhancements arise naturally from SPAWs rather than localized jets, providing direct observational evidence for anisotropic radial evolution of SPAWs in the inner heliosphere.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of Alfvén waves in solar wind acceleration and plasma heating, particularly to explain the observed one-sided radial velocity enhancement (Gosling boost) in large-amplitude Spherically Polarized Alfvén Waves seen by Parker Solar Probe.
AI.method: Starting from MHD equations, the authors derive the modified wave pressure and Poynting flux under the SPAW condition. Using PSP data from Encounters 6-25, they define an unperturbed velocity baseline via a lower 10th-percentile running average and statistically characterize the radial evolution of Alfvénic fluctuations.
AI.result: The background solar wind velocity shows clear radial acceleration, while the velocity perturbation amplitude δv decreases with heliocentric distance. This decay is anisotropic between radial and perpendicular directions, directly resulting from the growing magnetic deflection angle related to spherical polarization.
AI.conclusion: Radial velocity enhancements in the young solar wind arise naturally from SPAWs rather than from localized velocity jets, and the study provides direct observational evidence for the anisotropic radial evolution of SPAWs in the inner heliosphere.
